Mr. Vijay D. Patil, Psi, Powai Police Station, Present.
Coram:- N. J. Jamadar, J.

DATED:- 18th DECEMBER, 2023 P.C:-
1) Heard the learned Counsel for the applicant and the learned APP for the State.

2) This application is preferred for pre-arrest bail  connection with C.R. No. 288 of 2023, registered with Powai Police Station, Mumbai for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("the Penal Code").

sentences.text: The applicant deals in the business of scrap under the name and style of "Ocean Pearl".
The first informant also deals in the said business.
The first informant lodged the report with the allegations that the applicant induced the first informant to part with an amount of Rs.22,20,000/- and misappropriated the same.

4) The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant had, in turn, placed orders with the suppliers Pee Grinding Ltd and Motiwala Corporation and transferred the amount received from the first informant to those suppliers.
The suppliers did not deliver the goods.
Therefore, there was default.

5) The learned Counsel for the applicant seeks leave to tender a compilation, which consists of documents evidencing placing of orders by the applicant with the suppliers and the correspondence which ensued upon the failure to deliver the supplies of the goods.
Leave granted.
6) The learned APP, in the backdrop of the submissions advanced and the documents tendered, seeks time to take instructions.

sentences.text: 23.DOC
7) Mr. Singh, the learned Counsel submits that he has instructions to appear on behalf of the first informant.
The learned Counsel submits that the applicant has deceived the first informant.
8) In the backdrop of the nature of the accusation, it may be expedient to implead the first informant as a party respondent to this application.
9) Necessary amendment be carried out forthwith.
10) Issue notice to the respondents, returnable on 6 February, 2024.
11) Mr. Yadav, the learned APP waives notice to respondent No. 1.
12) Mr. Singh, the learned Counsel waives notice to respondent No. 2.

13) A pivotal question that warrants consideration is, whether the intention of the applicant was dishonest since the inception of the transaction or was it a case of failure on the part of the applicant to sell and deliver the goods as promised, entailing civil liability.

Since the applicant has placed documents, which prima facie indicate that the applicant had, in turn, placed orders with the suppliers and credited the amount to the  3/5 Chandrika Padmanabhi vs State Of Maharashtra on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135955103/

sentences.text: 14) Hence, the following order:-

ORDER I) In the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with C.R. No. 288 of 2023, registered with Powai Police Station, Mumbai for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860, the applicant be released on bail on executing a PR Bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- with one or two sureties in the like amount.

II) The applicant shall co-operate with the investigation and attend Powai Police Station, Mumbai on 28th and 29th December, 2023 in between 10.00 am to 1.00 pm and, thereafter, as and when directed by the Investigating Officer.
III) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence and/or give threat or inducement to the first informant and any of the persons acquainted with the facts of the case.

25-ABA-3419-23.DOC IV) The respondent No. 2 is at liberty to file an affidavit-in- reply and serve its copy on the applicant on or before next date.
V) Stand over to 6th February, 2024.
[N. J. JAMADAR, J.]
